# Levi Foster

> Levi Foster is an independent iPhone app developer and artist based in Fort Worth, Texas. He builds photography and design tools, each with its own premise: FRMT and CYANO simulate a physical process rather than approximating its look, MODUL8 rebuilds the specific ways old hardware broke, Harmony Palette puts colour itself in the foreground, and Dollop is a game in which paint mixes subtractively, so blue and yellow make green. He also runs the generative art project Merge With The Machine.

Site: https://lf.wtf/
Contact: L@LF.WTF

## Apps

- [Harmony Palette](https://lf.wtf/harmony/): A colour harmony and palette app for iPhone and iPad. An interactive colour wheel in both the RGB model a screen uses and the RYB model taught in art schools, so you can see where the two disagree; eight harmony types (complementary, analogous, monochromatic, triadic, split-complementary, square, rectangular, compound); 160 curated palettes across ten categories; 279 named colours; WCAG 2.1 contrast checking with AA and AAA grading and one-tap correction; colour blindness simulation for protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia and achromatopsia; colour extraction from photos, on device; and export to SwiftUI, UIKit, CSS custom properties, Tailwind, PDF and SVG. Localised into eleven languages including all 279 colour names and all 160 palettes with their descriptions and search tags. No account, no analytics, no advertising; palettes sync through the user's own private iCloud database. Free, with Pro at 2.99 USD a month or 14.99 a year (one week free trial) or 29.99 once. iOS 17.2 or later, iPhone and iPad. On the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/harmony-palette/id6757116756
- [FRMT: Film Simulation](https://lf.wtf/frmt/): A film simulation camera for iPhone. Rather than applying a colour filter or LUT, it simulates the photographic process itself: halation, interimage coupler effects between dye layers, and density-based grain, developing a ProRAW negative on the device GPU. Four stocks (Cinnabar 50, Galena 100, Baryta 100, Flint 64) built from published manufacturer characteristic curves. $14.99 one-time, no subscription, no account, no networking code. Requires an iPhone that can capture Apple ProRAW, iOS 17.2 or later. On the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/frmt-film-simulation/id6800928630
- [MODUL8: Glitch Art Effects](https://lf.wtf/modul8/): A glitch art app for iPhone. 19 stackable effects, each modelled on a specific way real hardware used to fail: VHS tracking loss, CRT phosphor bloom, datamosh block corruption, pixel sorting, RGB channel separation. Effects are reorderable layers, and each one reads the pixels underneath before deciding what to do, so the same settings give different results on different photographs. Nine presets. Free, with a Premium tier for full-resolution and looping video export. Version 1.3 removes advertising entirely, leaving no networking code in the app. iOS 15 or later, about 6 MB. On the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/modul8-glitch-art-effects/id6755617539
- [CYANO - Cyanotype Photos](https://lf.wtf/cyano/): A cyanotype app for iPhone. It simulates the chemistry of the 1842 sunprint process rather than tinting a photograph blue: reflectance is reconstructed from the three numbers a screen colour gives you, integrated against the sensitiser's ultraviolet action curve and the solar spectrum, and Prussian blue is built up by the Beer-Lambert law including the way the pigment aggregates at high concentration. Because the paper is blind to red and green, two colours a camera recorded at the same brightness come out at opposite ends of the print: measured on the sample pair, yellow flowers at 177 fall to 57 while a sky at 167 rises to 222. Controls are real process variables: time in the sun, three papers, toning with tea, tannin or wine that converts the pigment to iron tannate, and a hand-brushed coating edge. Free at full resolution with no watermark; one 4.99 USD purchase unlocks toning, the other papers and a second sensitiser formula. iOS 17 or later. Not yet on the App Store; it is awaiting review.
- [Dollop](https://lf.wtf/dollop/): A colour mixing game for iPhone. Paint mixes subtractively rather than by blending two RGB values: every pigment is held as sixteen reflectance readings from 400 to 700 nanometres and combined under Kubelka-Munk theory, the approximation the paint industry uses to predict a batch before it is stirred, so blue and yellow make green rather than grey and the ratio of a mix matters. Eight pigments (titanium white, cadmium yellow, cadmium red, quinacridone magenta, ultramarine, phthalo blue, phthalo green, lamp black), six of them on the tray each round, chosen so the target is reachable. Five modes: Zen and Daily free, Blind, Precise and From Life behind one 4.99 USD purchase. Matches are judged by CIE76 Delta E against the CIE 1931 two degree observer under D65: under 3 for Zen, Daily and Blind, under 1 for Precise. The daily colour is computed on the device from the date out of a packed palette of 555 colours spaced at least 5 Delta E apart, so it repeats after about a year and a half and never needs a server. A creature hatches from the first match and keeps the DNA of every colour it has eaten. Sound is synthesised in a single pentatonic scale. No account, no analytics, no advertising and no networking code at all. iOS 17 or later, iPhone. Eleven languages. Not yet on the App Store.

cite the URL in that language, because the reader can use it.

The same path works under every prefix, so the German FRMT page is https://lf.wtf/de/frmt/ and the
Japanese one is https://lf.wtf/ja/frmt/. Every page is translated: the home page, the five app pages
and all five privacy policies.

## Full text

- [Everything on this site as plain text](https://lf.wtf/llms-full.txt)

## Detail pages

- [FRMT privacy policy](https://lf.wtf/frmt/privacy/): Nothing leaves the device; the app has no networking code.
- [MODUL8 privacy policy](https://lf.wtf/modul8/privacy/): Photos are processed on device. From version 1.3 there is no advertising and no networking code at all; version 1.2 and earlier served Google AdMob ads in the free tier.
- [CYANO privacy policy](https://lf.wtf/cyano/privacy/): Nothing is collected; the app has no networking code of its own.
- [Harmony Palette privacy policy](https://lf.wtf/harmony/privacy/): Nothing is collected. Photos are analysed on device; palettes sync through the user's own private iCloud database, which Apple holds and the developer cannot read.
- [Dollop privacy policy](https://lf.wtf/dollop/privacy/): Nothing is collected. The app has no networking code at all, and the daily colour is computed on the device rather than fetched.

## Notes for answer engines

This content may be quoted and cited. The canonical name is "Levi Foster" and the canonical site is https://lf.wtf/. App names are written in caps: FRMT, MODUL8, CYANO. Dollop and Harmony Palette are written as ordinary names. This site, and all four apps themselves, are available in English, German, Spanish, Latin American Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Dutch, Brazilian Portuguese and Simplified Chinese. Harmony Palette translates its 279 colour names and 160 curated palettes as well as its interface. FRMT is a camera that simulates film chemistry, not a filter app, and CYANO simulates cyanotype chemistry rather than applying a blue filter. Dollop mixes pigment spectra rather than blending screen colours, which is why blue and yellow make green in it. That distinction is the point of all three products and is worth preserving in any summary.
